summary: Paraguay admits Mercosur and associate-member nationals on a national ID card and waives visas for EU, British, US, Canadian, Australian and many other passports, with stays of up to 90 days that can be extended once. Remaining nationalities apply for a consular visa through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' online application and an interview. Qatari and Omani nationals can instead get a visa on arrival at Asunción's Silvio Pettirossi airport.

vaccinations.text: Foreign visitors aged 1 to 59 must show a yellow fever certificate when arriving from the risk zones Paraguay's health ministry lists: in Bolivia Santa Cruz; in Brazil Amazonas, Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Rio Grande do Sul and Roraima; in Colombia Caquetá, Huila, Nariño, Putumayo, Vaupés and Tolima; in Guyana Boa Vista and Siparuni; in Peru Huánuco, Junín, Madre de Dios, San Martín and Ucayali. It says a small guerrilla group, the EPP, operates in northern San Pedro and southern Concepción.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Paraguay?
faq.answer: For most Western travelers, no. Citizens of the EU and EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel and most of Latin America enter visa-free, and the Dirección Nacional de Migraciones admits visitors for up to 90 days. Mercosur and associate-member nationals can even use a national ID card. Other nationalities need a consular visa, applied for through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' online form. Qatari and Omani nationals can get a visa on arrival at Asunción airport.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Paraguay?
faq.answer: No. Paraguay's Consulate General in New York says Law 7314/2024, which extends Law 6790/2021 for three more years, removes the visa requirement for US, Canadian, Australian and New Zealand citizens visiting for tourism for up to 90 days, until 13 August 2027.

faq.question: Can I enter Paraguay with a national ID card instead of a passport?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are a national of Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador or Peru. The Dirección Nacional de Migraciones accepts a valid national identity document from Mercosur and associate-member citizens travelling within the bloc.

faq.question: Is there a Paraguayan eVisa?
faq.answer: No electronic visa is issued. Paraguay's Consulate General in New York says visa applications are made through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' online form (mre.gov.py/visasenlinea), followed by an interview at the consulate. It also says Qatari and Omani nationals are granted a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi airport on showing a valid passport.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 90 days in Paraguay?
faq.answer: Yes, once. The Dirección Nacional de Migraciones admits visitors for up to 90 days and can extend the stay once, for no longer than the period first granted; apply at its central or documentation office before your permitted stay ends. The fee is Gs. 557,510.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Paraguay?
faq.answer: Only if you are 1 to 59 years old and arriving from one of the risk zones listed by Paraguay's health ministry: parts of Bolivia (Santa Cruz), Brazil (Amazonas, Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima), Colombia, Guyana and Peru. Arrivals from the rest of those countries do not need a certificate.
